purpose: Synthetic scenario pack showing how a control plane can explain allowed, denied, approval-required, blocked, and retired-source AI governance outcomes.

scenarios.title: Allowed low-risk tool call
scenarios.narrative: A governed knowledge agent requests a low-risk read action using an approved tool, valid session metadata, and available budget.
scenarios.controlImplication: The platform can explain why a low-risk action was eligible to proceed without recording tool payloads or prompt text.

scenarios.title: Denied unapproved tool call
scenarios.narrative: An agent session requests a tool outside the approved allowlist, so runtime governance denies the action before execution.
scenarios.controlImplication: The platform can show least-privilege enforcement for tool access without running the requested tool.

scenarios.title: High-impact action requires approval
scenarios.narrative: A high-impact action reaches the governance layer and pauses for human approval before any runtime action can continue.
scenarios.controlImplication: The platform can separate automated policy checks from human-owned approval for higher-risk actions.

scenarios.title: Capability blocked before runtime
scenarios.narrative: A reusable capability fails synthetic scan evidence, so the admission decision blocks it before any agent can use it at runtime.
scenarios.controlImplication: The platform can govern what an agent may install or access before runtime policy evaluates a specific action.

scenarios.title: Retired RAG source blocked
scenarios.narrative: A knowledge source is retired, so it is no longer eligible to contribute to new governed RAG answers or citations.
scenarios.controlImplication: The platform can make source lifecycle state part of retrieval governance before producing new knowledge-grounded responses.
